Earth ReGen

Support This Demo

The planet is a rubbish tip. You start with one volunteer and your bare hands.

Earth ReGen is a factory-building incremental. Machines have typed sockets for workforce, energy and 13 kinds of material, and nothing runs until you wire them together. Packets run along every wire, so you can see where a line is starving.

A few games got me here: Upload Labs for the wiring, Satisfactory for building a factory, and The Planet Crafter for a dead world you bring back.

The free demo

  • 32 machines, 27 unlocks and 51 upgrades.
  • Two places to clean up. The ground changes as you clear it.
  • Weather: rain doubles your trees and halves your digging, and a storm puts every fire out.
  • 41 objectives, a guided first run, and a Plan that tells you what to do next.
  • Three save slots, save export, and progress while the tab is closed.
  • English and Russian (русский язык, in Settings).

The demo ends a few hours in, when you raise your first array at a Grid Foundry.

The full game

It is in development and coming to Steam, with five places, 80 machines, 100 upgrades, 100 achievements, and Trials that unlock rare machines. The trailer shows it.

Controls

  • To pick up rubbish by hand, move the cursor into a tip, out, and back in.
  • Drag from socket to socket to run a wire. Right-click a wire to cut it.
  • Shift-click to select several machines and drag them together.
  • Wheel or drag the map to zoom and pan. T opens the skill trees.

Before you start

  • Made for a desktop browser and a mouse.
  • Needs Chrome or Edge 111+, Firefox 126+ or Safari 16.4+.
  • Your save lives in your browser. Use EXPORT on the save slot to keep a copy.

Generative AI was used to build this game. AI wrote the code and some of the in-game text, in English and in Russian, from my design and my direction. The game design, the mechanics, the balance and the testing are mine. The music is mine. There is no generated art in the build: every machine icon, every cursor and the whole map is drawn in code.

It's free. If you finished the demo, or stopped somewhere and can say where, the comments are open.

saulrh6 days ago
  • Needs a system for sensors and controllers - time-varying stuff like the weather and the grid foundry/outreach hub don't have a fixed ratio that can be set ahead of time. "Switch power to the other trash pile when the first one is depleted" would also be a huge improvement.
  • Needs a better way to set ratios. A simple option would be wider splitters - having to think through splitting off N units of power at every splitter and passing on M-N is much more difficult than necessary.
  • Need better ways to show what's backing up/off-ratio in a production pipeline. For example, you could color the storage bar on a battery plant to show that it's holding some amount of aluminum and some amount of batteries and waiting on hazardous waste.
  • It's possible to softlock yourself by depleting your trash piles while selling the outputs instead of spending them on CI.
  • Once you get the outreach hub it's trivial to accumulate so much workforce that you'll never worry about it again, because the outreach hub's workers are the only thing in the entire game that cost _only_ workforce and energy and don't depend on anything that comes out of the trash pile.
  • Lines can only be highlighted/canceled at a few specific points along their length rather than along the whole curve. It's much easier to delete lines by clicking their endpoints than it is to delete them by clicking them directly.

Thanks, this is a really useful list.

The wires: you're right, and it's a bug. A curved wire only picks up clicks near a handful of points along it, so on a long wire most of it can't be clicked. I'll fix it so the whole wire works.

Switching power when a pile runs out: the full game has priority splitters for exactly that. They feed one side first and send everything to the other side once the first can't use it. They aren't in the demo though.

The softlock: I tried to cover it. When the Wastelands run dry, Greenhaven opens for free, and if every place in the demo is bare the Plan finishes for you. The full game also has Clean Index makers that don't need trash at all.

Outreach Hub: fair. It's the one workforce source that needs nothing from the trash. There's a cap of 10 and each recruit costs more than the last, but I'll look at whether it's still too easy.

Wider splitters and showing what's backing up: both good ideas and I've written them down. The cards do name a missing input already, but a bar that shows what's actually sitting inside would be much clearer.

Sensors and controllers is a bigger one. I like it, but I can't promise it yet.

Disagreeg32 days ago

Good to know the splitter version works, and thanks for saying which shape you ended up with.

I want to check the loop detection idea before I agree with it, because I do not think there is any. As far as I know nothing in the game refuses a loop or zeroes one. So if a direct loop went dead there is probably another reason, and I would rather find it than guess at it.

One thing worth trying while I look. An outreach centre needs workforce and energy together. If it runs short of energy it banks workforce until it cannot hold any more, then deliberately holds its own input cable so the workforce goes somewhere useful instead. From outside that looks exactly like the line dying for no reason. If your block is tight on power, that could be it rather than the wiring. Worth watching whether the ones that go quiet are the ones furthest from your generators.

That is a guess until I have sat down with your shape though, so treat it as something to try rather than an answer.

Either way, if a machine can hold its own cable and say nothing about it, that is on me and not on your wiring. It should tell you.
